draft.title: Solids, liquids and gases
card: Solid
The particles are packed close together in a fixed pattern. They vibrate in place but do not move past each other.
Liquid
The particles are close together but not in a fixed pattern. They slide past each other, so a liquid can flow and take the shape of its container.
Gas
The particles are far apart and move freely in all directions. A gas spreads out to fill its container.

Because gas particles have a lot of space between them, they can be pushed closer together. This is why a gas can be squashed. Solid and liquid particles are already close, so they are very hard to squash.
draft.remember: The closer the particles and the less freely they move, the more fixed the substance.

a.q: Which sentence correctly describes the particles in a liquid?
opts: They are close together and slide past each other
They are close together and vibrate in a fixed place
They are far apart and move freely in all directions
They are far apart and slide past each other slowly
a.why: Liquid particles are close together but can slide past each other, which lets a liquid flow. Vibrating in a fixed place describes a solid, because solid particles cannot move past their neighbours.
a.clue: Think about what lets a liquid be poured.

b.q: Zoe pushes the plunger of a sealed syringe. The syringe full of air can be squashed a lot, but one full of water hardly changes. Why?
opts: Air particles are far apart, so they can be pushed closer
Air particles are smaller, so they take up less room
Water particles are far apart, so they cannot be pushed
Water particles vibrate in place, so they are packed tighter
b.why: Gas particles have a lot of space between them, so pushing the plunger moves them closer together. Water particles are already close together, so there is little space to squash into. The idea that water particles vibrate in place describes a solid, not a liquid.
b.clue: Compare how much space is between the particles in each.

a.best: They are close together and slide past each other

b.best: Air particles are far apart, so they can be pushed closer

problems.detail: The remember line suggests a scale where closer particles mean a more fixed substance. The card says solid and liquid particles are both close together, and that what makes a solid fixed is its fixed pattern, not closeness. A student could wrongly conclude that solid particles are much closer than liquid particles. 'More fixed' is also vague.

check.summary: Both questions and their explanations are correct, with one clear right answer each. The remember line implies closeness is what makes a solid fixed, which blurs the card's point that solids and liquids are both close-packed.
